folds.title: Four simple habits
points: A few habits make most prompts better.
None needs special words or tricks.
Meet each one, then see it at work.

folds.title: Show an example
points: Paste one sample of what you like, such as a past email.
Claude copies a style far better from an example than from a description.

chat.you: Write a book club invite. Match the tone of last year's: "Books, snacks and gossip! Join us Friday at 7."

chat.claude: Pages, pastries and plot twists! Join us Saturday at 6.

folds.title: Ask for steps
points: For a tricky question or a budget, say "work through it step by step".
So you can spot a wrong turn.

folds.title: Asking for steps

chat.you: I earn 2,000 a month and spend 1,700. Step by step: can I save 500?

chat.claude: 1. That leaves 300. 2. 500 is 200 more. 3. Not yet: trim 200 of spending first.

folds.note: Each step is easy to check.

folds.title: Add structure
points: Put long material in clear, labelled blocks.
Like "Here is my draft:" then "Here is what I want changed:".
It stops Claude mixing them up.

folds.title: Adding structure
folds.note: Claude knows which part is which.

folds.title: Iterate
points: Your first prompt is a first try.
Read the answer, then say what to change.
Chatting back and forth is the normal way to work.

chat.you: Suggest a name for my bakery.
Nice! Something warmer, with my name, Rosa.

folds.prompt: Tap each card to flip it from weak to strong.

cards.weak: Write an email to my landlord.
cards.strong: Write a polite email to my landlord about a leaking tap. Here is an email I wrote before, copy its friendly tone: ...
Here is my monthly budget: ... Go through it step by step and tell me where I overspend.
cards.note: Asks for steps and labels the material.
